**Date:** 2026-06-12  
**Source:** [OpenAI — New OpenAI Academy courses for the next era of work](https://openai.com/index/academy-courses-applying-ai-at-work)

## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools

**Date:** 2026-06-11  
**Source:** [MiniMax — M3](https://www.minimax.io/models/text/m3)  
**Summary:** MiniMax introduced M3, an open-weight coding and agentic model with native multimodality, MiniMax Sparse Attention, and API support for up to a 1M-token context window.  
**Why it matters:** Adds another long-context open-weight entrant for coding, browsing, and agent workflows, increasing pressure on closed coding-agent stacks.

**Date:** 2026-06-12  
**Source:** [TechCrunch — Avataar launches Varya](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/11/cheaper-faster-and-culturally-aware-avataars-video-ai-is-built-for-indias-scale/)  
**Summary:** Avataar launched Varya, a lower-cost India-focused video-generation model distilled from Alibaba’s Wan 2.2, with open-weight release planned via India’s AIKosh portal.  
**Why it matters:** Regionally optimized video models are moving from generic global systems toward localized language, culture, and cost constraints.

## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics

**Date:** 2026-06-12  
**Source:** [AI Daily Brief — 10 Sites Knowledge Workers Should Build with AI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=45UGHbqq2fQ)  
**Summary:** The episode argues that many knowledge-work outputs should become living, shareable sites rather than static decks, memos, spreadsheets, reports, proposals, or training documents. It cites OpenAI’s Codex “Sites” feature as the enabling tool.  
**Workflow:**  
1. Pick a static work artifact: report, proposal, dashboard, training guide, or client memo.  
2. Use Codex/Sites to convert it into an interactive web page.  
3. Add navigable sections, embedded tables, scenario views, filters, or calculators.  
4. Share as a link instead of sending a file.  
5. Update the site as facts, metrics, or decisions change.  
**Available now:** Yes, per the podcast source.  
**Why it matters:** The tactical shift is from one-time document production to maintained operational surfaces that teams can revisit, update, and use directly.
